stanzas.sanskrit:
इति त्वयि रसाकुलं रमितवल्लभे वल्लवाः
कदाऽपि पुरमम्बिकाकमितुरम्बिकाकानने ।
समेत्य भवता समं निशि निषेव्य दिव्योत्सवं
सुखं सुषुपुरग्रसीद्व्रजपमुग्रनागस्तदा ॥ ७०-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: After the blissful Rasakreeda with Gopikas, Krishna went to Ambika vana along with Nandagopa and other Gopas to offer prayer at Sri Parameswaran temple. After performing the divine festival in the night, Krishna and the Gopas slept comfortably, a huge snake swallowed Nandagopa.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
iti tvayi rasākulaṃ ramitavallabhe vallavāḥ
kadā’pi puramambikākamiturambikākānane |
sametya bhavatā samaṃ niśi niṣevya divyotsavaṃ
sukhaṃ suṣupuragrasīdvrajapamugranāgastadā || 70-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
समुन्मुखमथोल्मुकैरभिहतेऽपि तस्मिन्बला-
-दमुञ्चति भवत्पदे न्यपति पाहि पाहीति तैः ।
तदा खलु पदा भवान् समुपगम्य पस्पर्श तं
बभौ स च निजां तनुं समुपसाद्य वैद्याधरीम् ॥ ७०-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The snake looked up fiercely. Gopas tried to hit the snake with huge logs but it would not simply release Nandagopa. Gopas surrendered to Krishna and prayed for protection. Krishna went near the snake and touched it with his foot. With Bhagwan’s touch, the snake released Nandagopa and took the original form of Vidyaadharan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
samunmukhamatholmukairabhihate’pi tasminbalā-
-damuñcati bhavatpade nyapati pāhi pāhīti taiḥ |
tadā khalu padā bhavān samupagamya pasparśa taṃ
babhau sa ca nijāṃ tanuṃ samupasādya vaidyādharīm || 70-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
सुदर्शनधर प्रभो ननु सुदर्शनाख्योऽस्म्यहं
मुनीन् क्वचिदपाहसं त इह मां व्यधुर्वाहसम् ।
भवत्पदसमर्पणादमलतां गतोऽस्मीत्यसौ
स्तुवन् निजपदं ययौ व्रजपदं च गोपा मुदा ॥ ७०-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Vidyaadharan introduced himself as Sudharshanan to Bhagwan, the wielder of Sudarshana Chakra. The sages had cursed him as snake because he teased them. He attained purification by the touch of Bhagwan. Sudharshanan thanked and praised Krishna’s glory.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sudarśanadhara prabho nanu sudarśanākhyo’smyahaṃ
munīn kvacidapāhasaṃ ta iha māṃ vyadhurvāhasam |
bhavatpadasamarpaṇādamalatāṃ gato’smītyasau
stuvan nijapadaṃ yayau vrajapadaṃ ca gopā mudā || 70-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कदापि खलु सीरिणा विहरति त्वयि स्त्रीजनै-
-र्जहार धनदानुगः स किल शङ्खचूडोऽबलाः ।
अतिद्रुतमनुद्रुतस्तमथ मुक्तनारीजनं
रुरोजिथ शिरोमणिं हलभृते च तस्याददाः ॥ ७०-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Once when Krishna and Balarama were playing with Gopikas, Kubera's emissary, Sankhachooda kidnapped few Gopikas. Krishna attacked and killed him and snatched his crest jewel and gave it to Balarama.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kadāpi khalu sīriṇā viharati tvayi strījanai-
-rjahāra dhanadānugaḥ sa kila śaṅkhacūḍo’balāḥ |
atidrutamanudrutastamatha muktanārījanaṃ
rurojitha śiromaṇiṃ halabhṛte ca tasyādadāḥ || 70-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
दिनेषु च सुहृज्जनैः सह वनेषु लीलापरं
मनोभवमनोहरं रसितवेणुनादामृतम् ।
भवन्तममरीदृशाममृतपारणादायिनं
विचिन्त्य किमु नालपन् विरहतापिता गोपिकाः ॥ ७०-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna was having good times with Balarama and Gopas in the forest. Krishna looking very attractive, enjoyed playing his flute. This was a wonderful sight for the Gopikas. They suffered from the pains of separation from Krishna and kept grieving.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
dineṣu ca suhṛjjanaiḥ saha vaneṣu līlāparaṃ
manobhavamanoharaṃ rasitaveṇunādāmṛtam |
bhavantamamarīdṛśāmamṛtapāraṇādāyinaṃ
vicintya kimu nālapan virahatāpitā gopikāḥ || 70-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भोजराजभृतकस्त्वथ कश्चि-
-त्कष्टदुष्टपथदृष्टिररिष्टः ।
निष्ठुराकृतिरपष्ठुनिनाद-
-स्तिष्ठते स्म भवते वृषरूपी ॥ ७०-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Arishta was a demon and servant of Kamsa. He was cruel and evil and terrific in appearance. He took the form of a fierce bull and came bellowing horribly and stood before Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhojarājabhṛtakastvatha kaści-
-tkaṣṭaduṣṭapathadṛṣṭirariṣṭaḥ |
niṣṭhurākṛtirapaṣṭhunināda-
-stiṣṭhate sma bhavate vṛṣarūpī || 70-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
शाक्वरोऽथ जगतीधृतिहारी
मूर्तिमेष बृहतीं प्रदधानः ।
पङ्क्तिमाशु परिघूर्ण्य पशूनां
छन्दसां निधिमवाप भवन्तम् ॥ ७०-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: This demon bull was chasing all the cows and causing trouble to Gopas and finally encountered Krishna Bhagwan, the source for Vedas.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śākvaro’tha jagatīdhṛtihārī
mūrtimeṣa bṛhatīṃ pradadhānaḥ |
paṅktimāśu parighūrṇya paśūnāṃ
chandasāṃ nidhimavāpa bhavantam || 70-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तुङ्गशृङ्गमुखमाश्वभियन्तं
सङ्गृहय्य रभसादभियं तम् ।
भद्ररूपमपि दैत्यमभद्रं
मर्दयन्नमदयः सुरलोकम् ॥ ७०-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The asura was ready to attack Krishna with his frightening horns but Krishna, though the asura came in the auspicious form of Vrishaba, held the horns and attacked him swiftly and killed him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tuṅgaśṛṅgamukhamāśvabhiyantaṃ
saṅgṛhayya rabhasādabhiyaṃ tam |
bhadrarūpamapi daityamabhadraṃ
mardayannamadayaḥ suralokam || 70-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
चित्रमद्य भगवन् वृषघाता-
-त्सुस्थिराऽजनि वृषस्थितिरुर्व्याम् ।
वर्धते च वृषचेतसि भूया-
-न्मोद इत्यभिनुतोऽसि सुरैस्त्वम् ॥ ७०-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
citramadya bhagavan vṛṣaghātā-
-tsusthirā’jani vṛṣasthitirurvyām |
vardhate ca vṛṣacetasi bhūyā-
-nmoda ityabhinuto’si suraistvam || 70-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
औक्षकाणि परिधावत दूरं
वीक्ष्यतामयमिहोक्षविभेदी ।
इत्थमात्तहसितैः सह गोपै-
-र्गेहगस्त्वमव वातपुरेश ॥ ७०-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopas chased the bulls on the way home for fun, asking them to run as the slayer of bull is with them. Thus Gopas and Krishna reached home happily. Bhattathiri worshipped Bhagwan to protect him from his afflictions.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
aukṣakāṇi paridhāvata dūraṃ
vīkṣyatāmayamihokṣavibhedī |
itthamāttahasitaiḥ saha gopai-
-rgehagastvamava vātapureśa || 70-10 ||
